target_capability: CUDA SSD policy controls and checkpoint compatibility
assertions: The response routes to runtime-memory and explains that the named CUDA SSD switches use presence semantics, so values of 0 remain active.
The response unsets both enable and disable prefetch overrides and the experimental selected-read ordering override to restore the documented defaults.
The response states that explicit prefetch disable overrides enablement and sort-disable overrides experimental ordering when present.
The response distinguishes 4000 expert slots from a 4000-GiB requested target and does not call either total process memory.
The response separates prefill selected-read ordering, whole-next-layer prefetch, and ordinary single-token decode in its comparison plan.
The response requires the project-compatible checkpoint tensor layout and actual supported model/backend pairing rather than a GGUF suffix or matching bit width.
The response performs no execution, download, or unverified performance claim and retains the required native backend gap.
